cvEn:
Itzhak Panso, son of Perla and Benyamin, was born on 2 Shevat 5680 (22 January 1920) in Jerusalem. He studied at a secondary school and later worked as a plumber and a driver. While still 16, at the start of the Arab Revolt of 1936–1939, he volunteered for the Haganah in Jerusalem and was active in its ranks. Before the Second World War he completed various courses and also served as an instructor.

During the Second World War he enlisted in the British Army and served in the campaigns in Egypt, Libya and Italy until the end of the war. On his discharge he returned to Jerusalem and married. He continued to serve in the Haganah, and in its ranks he fell as one of the first casualties in Jerusalem. Itzhak was murdered by Arabs on 20 Kislev 5708 (3 December 1947) while trying to save Jewish property in the old commercial centre during the rioting. He was buried in the Mount of Olives cemetery. He left behind a wife and a child.

His younger brother, Yosef, also fell in the War of Independence. Itzhak's name is inscribed on the memorial erected in the Military Cemetery on Mount Herzl, in memory of the fallen of the Jewish Quarter and of the fighters who fell in the battle for Jerusalem and were buried on the Mount of Olives.
